outcomes.description: Member found; summary shows Name and accounts table. Read name from the 'Name:' value cell and the balance from the row whose Description is 'Share Savings'.
Search ran but no member exists with the given member number; no name/balance to extract.
App-side validation rejected the member number (e.g. not 5 digits / non-numeric); search form redisplayed with an error.
Teller lacks permission to view this (restricted) member; details cannot be read.
A member alert interstitial appears after search requiring a person to read and confirm identity; replay must hand off to a human, then continue to member_detail.
Application error page (fatal) during search; flow cannot complete and must be retried later.

input.notes:
Flow is read-only. The app is a frameset: the search form and results both render in the right-hand content iframe; the left nav iframe has Member Inquiry / Sign Off links.

Steps: type the member number into the Member ID textbox, click Search, then read the two values off the Member Summary screen.

Extraction locators (positional refs may shift between runs):
- member_name: the value cell in the row labelled "Name:" of the summary table.
- share_savings_balance: the Balance cell of the accounts-table row whose Description is "Share Savings" (suffix 00). Do NOT take the first data row blindly — account ordering/suffixes can vary; match on the "Share Savings" description. Other rows such as "Share Draft Checking" must be ignored.

This run: member «inputs.member_id» -> «member_name», «share_savings_balance».

Interstitials expected on other runs: system_notice (dismiss), service_unavailable (retry), session_expired / signed_out (cannot be self-handled — no credentials may be entered; escalate). member_alert is deliberately NOT auto-dismissed and requires request_help before continuing to member_detail.

The member_detail screen also offers "Open Sub-Account" (leading to subacct_form / subacct_review / subacct_opened / subacct_invalid). Those states are out of scope for this read-only lookup and were not exercised; never click that link during replay.
